newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to raise size of bond auction on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to raise size of bond auction on Friday.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Wednesday that it would raise the amount of one-month bonds to be auctioned on Friday, March 28, to 30 billion baht from two billion baht originally planned.

The move was being made to mop up excess liquidity that would hit the market following the scheduled launch of a 78 billion baht ($3 billion) Government Pension Fund (GPF) on Thursday, the central bank said in a statement.
The GPF is expected to flush the market with funds and push down interbank rates and the central bank had pledged to act to prevent any excessive swings in the rates through its repurchase window.
The central bank also said it would expand the list of eligible buyers of Bank of Thailand bonds from Thursday.
"Effective from Thursday (March 27), the list of eligible BOT bond buyers would be expanded to include the Government Pension Fund," it added.
"Members institutions of the Bank of Thailand's repurchase market which otherwise are not eligible buyers will also be permitted to buy BOT bonds in the repurchase market," it said.
Last Friday, the central bank auctioned 20 billion baht, up from an originally planned two billion baht.
